landing.architectureLead: NestJS adapters normalise kopiykas, millilitres and PascalCase before the data ever reaches the interface. A new vendor is a new adapter, not a new system.
landing.cap.analytics.desc: Spend over time, a breakdown by fuel type and a brand comparison for any date range.
landing.cap.analytics.long: Spend over time, by fuel type and across brands — on one screen and for any period you choose.
landing.cap.analytics.p0: OKKO and Shell compared on a shared time axis
landing.cap.analytics.p1: Breakdown by fuel type and station network
landing.cap.analytics.p2: Chart colours are read from the theme, not hardcoded
landing.cap.analytics.title: Spend analytics
landing.cap.cache.desc: Vendor responses are cached: the page paints from cache at once and fresh data arrives in the background.
landing.cap.cache.long: Vendors are slow to answer. So the page paints from cache instantly, and fresh data replaces it when it lands.
landing.cap.cache.p0: Cache younger than 30 seconds — no network request at all
landing.cap.cache.p1: Older but under 12 hours — shown at once, refreshed in the background
landing.cap.cache.p2: The cache survives a reload and is cleared on sign-out
landing.cap.cache.title: Instant start
landing.cap.dataModel.desc: Kopiykas, millilitres and PascalCase stay with the vendor — from outside all three APIs look the same.
landing.cap.dataModel.long: Every vendor has its own adapter. Downstream there is one schema, and a new vendor changes nothing in it.
landing.cap.dataModel.p0: Three different formats reduce to a single structure
landing.cap.dataModel.p1: A dead vendor yields an empty list, not a full-screen error
landing.cap.dataModel.p2: Pagination is computed in memory, because the vendors’ own paging is incompatible
landing.cap.dataModel.title: One data model
landing.cap.export.desc: Excel and PDF straight from the table on screen: currencies, volumes and dates are formatted automatically.
landing.cap.export.long: What you see in the table lands in Excel or PDF with the right column types — no manual formatting.
landing.cap.export.p0: Column type is inferred from its header
landing.cap.export.p1: Currencies, volumes and dates format themselves
landing.cap.export.p2: Action and status columns never reach the report
landing.cap.export.title: Report export
landing.cap.fuelCards.desc: OKKO and Shell in one window — transactions, cards, stations and limits without switching portals.
landing.cap.fuelCards.long: Two networks with incompatible APIs collapse into one journal. You see a refuelling, not the format its vendor returned.
landing.cap.fuelCards.p0: OKKO counts in kopiykas and millilitres — the conversion lives in the adapter
landing.cap.fuelCards.p1: Shell returns dates as YYYYMMDD and fields in PascalCase
landing.cap.fuelCards.p2: Price per litre is derived from amount and volume, not taken from the response
landing.cap.fuelCards.title: Fuel cards
landing.cap.i18n.desc: The language is resolved on the server with no flash, and a missing translation falls back to Ukrainian.
landing.cap.i18n.long: The server knows the language, so the first frame already arrives in it. Ukrainian remains the fallback for any key.
landing.cap.i18n.p0: The language lives in a cookie, not only in localStorage
landing.cap.i18n.p1: A missing translation shows Ukrainian, not the key name
landing.cap.i18n.p2: Number and date formats follow the chosen language
landing.cap.i18n.title: Ten languages
landing.cap.liveTrack.desc: Watch a single vehicle at intervals from 3 seconds, with the track building up on the map.
landing.cap.liveTrack.long: One tractor under watch: the track accumulates on the client and draws on the map while you look.
landing.cap.liveTrack.p1: Track window from 15 minutes to 3 hours
landing.cap.liveTrack.p2: An empty window widens to 24 hours instead of showing a blank map
landing.cap.liveTrack.title: Live tracking
landing.cap.maps.desc: Ten basemaps, satellite and topography, tile opacity, scale and coordinates under the cursor.
landing.cap.maps.long: Both maps share one set of preferences: basemap, tile legibility, and which controls exist at all.
landing.cap.maps.p0: Ten providers, including satellite and topography
landing.cap.maps.p1: Tile opacity, grayscale, brightness and contrast
landing.cap.maps.p2: The “auto” basemap follows the application theme
landing.cap.maps.title: Configurable maps
landing.cap.palette.desc: Jump between sections, themes and languages from the keyboard — ⌘K anywhere in the app.
landing.cap.palette.long: One hotkey for the whole app: move between sections, change theme and language, refresh data — without the mouse.
landing.cap.palette.p0: ⌘K works on any page of the application
landing.cap.palette.p1: Search across sections, themes and languages
landing.cap.palette.p2: Renders nothing until it is opened
landing.cap.palette.title: Command palette
landing.cap.roles.desc: Read-only demo access, enforced on the server rather than by hiding buttons.
landing.cap.roles.long: You can show a guest everything without worry: the write ban sits on the server, so it cannot be bypassed from the browser console.
landing.cap.roles.p0: Any non-GET request from a guest gets a 403
landing.cap.roles.p1: The interface only mirrors the rule, it does not create it
landing.cap.roles.p2: A trip from the dashboard hits a live API — which is why the guard is server-side
landing.cap.roles.title: Roles and guest mode
landing.cap.telematics.desc: Position, speed, ignition, RPM, engine hours and fuel level straight from the tractor CAN bus.
landing.cap.telematics.long: Data straight off the tractor bus: how much fuel is in the tank, whether the engine is running, how many engine hours are on it.
landing.cap.telematics.p0: Fuel level in litres and per cent from CAN
landing.cap.telematics.p2: A missing reading is null — not a zero and not a dash
landing.cap.telematics.title: Fleet telematics
landing.cap.trips.desc: Trip planning, loading and unloading points, driver assignment through Ruptela R&T.
landing.cap.trips.long: A trip is created in the dashboard and lands in the live Routing & Tasking API, not in a local list.
landing.cap.trips.p0: Loading and unloading points with cargo weight
landing.cap.trips.p1: The driver is resolved from the vehicle’s most recent trip
landing.cap.trips.p2: Creating a trip does not page a driver unless you ask it to
landing.cap.trips.title: Routes and trips

landing.exp.ctaLead: Sign in to the demo and look at live transactions, mileage and trips — with no placeholders anywhere.
landing.exp.heroLead: Fuel, mileage and trips arrive from three different APIs in three different formats. The platform reduces them to a single table — and shows what each kilometre actually cost.
landing.exp.liveShareNote: cost lines are already filled in automatically
landing.exp.norm0.note: The amount is divided by 100 inside the OKKO adapter. Downstream everything is hryvnias — with no place left to forget it.
landing.exp.norm1.note: Volume is divided by 1000 in the same place. The price per litre is not taken from the response — it is computed from amount and volume.
landing.exp.norm2.note: Shell dates are converted to ISO on the way in. Otherwise they end up as separate labels on the chart axis.
landing.exp.norm3.note: OKKO will not return a wider range. The start of the period is pulled forward instead of the request failing.
landing.exp.normLead: A kopiyka mistaken for a hryvnia, or a date in someone else’s format, costs more than it looks. These conversions live in the vendor adapter — and nowhere else.
landing.exp.normTitle: Accounting breaks on the small things

landing.heroLead: One interface for OKKO and Shell cards, Ruptela telematics and fleet routing. From the transaction to the track point.
landing.int.amic.what: Cards for legal entities: balances, transactions, fund transfers, card blocking.
landing.int.amic.why: Strong coverage in western Ukraine — where every run from Bukovina begins.
landing.int.basErp.what: An automatic OData REST interface to the reference data and documents of the accounting system.
landing.int.basErp.why: Accounting receives ready documents instead of re-keying statements by hand every month.
landing.int.cardAggregators.what: One card for 8+ networks: WOG, SOCAR, KLO, Ukrnafta, Shell, Marshal, Parallel.
landing.int.cardAggregators.why: Covers almost the whole market with one integration instead of six separate adapters.
landing.int.ecmr.what: The electronic international consignment note and digital transport-information exchange with EU authorities.
landing.int.ecmr.why: From July 2027 all competent EU authorities must accept this data digitally.
landing.int.ettn.what: The state system of electronic consignment notes via an accredited provider.
landing.int.ettn.why: Mandatory use is expected from 2027, and the fuel-specific forms start at the same time.
landing.int.flespi.what: Ingests data from 1000+ tracker protocols and serves it as one JSON over REST and MQTT.
landing.int.flespi.why: One adapter instead of separate code for every tracker that joins the fleet tomorrow.
landing.int.here.what: Routing that accounts for weight, height, axle load and ADR tunnel categories.
landing.int.here.why: For a tractor fleet that is the difference between a trip plan and a fine at a height-restricted bridge.
landing.int.medoc.what: The official module for exchanging primary documents and reporting with the accounting system.
landing.int.medoc.why: Installed in the vast majority of Ukrainian accounting departments — the shortest path to tax accounting.
landing.int.metabase.what: Self-hosted BI with dashboard embedding via a signed JWT.
landing.int.metabase.why: Deep analytics without trip data ever leaving your own server.
landing.int.monobank.what: Statements, balances and webhooks for new transactions with no request-rate limits.
landing.int.monobank.why: Webhooks update spend instantly, rather than once a day via a statement file.
landing.int.okko.what: Fuel cards, transactions, stations and card balances across the OKKO network.
landing.int.okko.why: The main network for domestic runs — the consolidated report started here.
landing.int.omnicomm.what: Sensors with the open LLS protocol over RS-232/RS-485 through the telematics unit.
landing.int.omnicomm.why: An alternative to Technoton on already-equipped tractors — independence from the previous contractor.
landing.int.opendatabot.what: Counterparty checks by EDRPOU code: registration data, tax debt, sanctions, director authority.
landing.int.opendatabot.why: Checks the customer before the truck leaves, not after an unpaid invoice.
landing.int.openweather.what: Forecasts along route points with road-surface temperature and black-ice risk.
landing.int.openweather.why: A warning about ice on a specific stretch, not about the weather in the city at large.
landing.int.ors.what: Open routing for heavy vehicles with dimensions and dangerous-goods type.
landing.int.ors.why: Free hypothesis testing until a paid HERE contract pays for itself.
landing.int.paperless.what: Free electronic document exchange, with integration offered as a separate service.
landing.int.paperless.why: Zero cost makes it the cheapest channel for small counterparties.
landing.int.powerbi.what: Push datasets with batches of up to 10,000 rows and service-principal authentication.
landing.int.powerbi.why: Fuel spend alongside the rest of the group's financial reporting.
landing.int.privatAutoclient.what: Statements, account balances and payment initiation via Privat24 for Business keys.
landing.int.privatAutoclient.why: Automatically matches fuel balance top-ups against bank debits.
landing.int.ruptelaFmTrack.what: Position, ignition, RPM, engine hours and fuel level from the tractor CAN bus.
landing.int.ruptelaFmTrack.why: Puts the physical truth of a run next to the financial one — consumption against payment.
landing.int.ruptelaRnt.what: Trip planning, loading and unloading points, driver assignment.
landing.int.ruptelaRnt.why: The task reaches the driver in the cab, not through a phone call with the dispatcher.
landing.int.saftUa.what: Export of accounting data into standardised OECD-format XML for the tax service e-audit.
landing.int.saftUa.why: Large taxpayers already file it, and fuel is a frequent source of questions during audits.
landing.int.shell.what: Shell card transactions from European stations in YYYYMMDD format.
landing.int.shell.why: Covers the international leg of a run, where Ukrainian cards are not accepted.
landing.int.socar.what: SOCAR network cards with a virtual equivalent and a client API for ERP synchronisation.
landing.int.socar.why: The only Ukrainian network after OKKO to state an API outright — the nearest third vendor.
landing.int.tachographDdd.what: Scheduled automatic download of tachograph and driver-card files through the Ruptela terminal already installed.
landing.int.tachographDdd.why: Removes the driver's trip to the office with a card and satisfies EU Regulation 165/2014.
landing.int.technoton.what: Capacitive level sensors and flow meters with 1% accuracy over the CAN J1939 bus.
landing.int.technoton.why: Tank volume next to the card transaction — that gap is exactly how siphoning gets caught.
landing.int.telegram.what: Notifications, reports and confirmation buttons for drivers and dispatchers.
landing.int.telegram.why: A free channel drivers already use daily — an alert lands in seconds.
landing.int.teltonika.what: Remote management of tracker configurations and firmware.
landing.int.teltonika.why: Hardware updates without calling the tractor back to the depot.
landing.int.ukrnafta.what: Cards and vouchers with a portal for transactions, spend analytics and reports.
landing.int.ukrnafta.why: The widest coverage in regions where OKKO and Shell are thin on the ground.
landing.int.upg.what: Electronic fuel cards and vouchers with real-time asset control.
landing.int.upg.why: Works actively with large fleets; API integration is mentioned for corporate customers.
landing.int.vchasno.what: An open API for exporting documents and sending new ones to a counterparty for signature.
landing.int.vchasno.why: Fuel acts and invoices are signed from the ERP, without a separate document-flow window.
landing.int.viber.what: Transactional messages with images and buttons via Infobip or Kyivstar.
landing.int.viber.why: The primary messenger for the drivers who never took to Telegram.
landing.int.visicom.what: Ukrainian cartography: geocoding, place search and routing across Ukraine and neighbouring countries.
landing.int.visicom.why: An address base more detailed than global services — more accurate placement of stations and unloading points.
landing.int.wialon.what: Objects, messages, reports and events from a platform supporting 3600+ tracker models.
landing.int.wialon.why: Lets you connect a fleet already running on Wialon without swapping a single tracker.
landing.int.wog.what: Smart cards and a B2B portal with limits, balances and invoices.
landing.int.wog.why: One of the largest networks — without it the consolidated fuel report is always incomplete.
landing.integrationsLead: What is already connected, what can be connected tomorrow — and where the Ukrainian market still offers no public API.
landing.integrationsNote: Most Ukrainian fuel networks publish no API — they have a customer portal but no documented interface. We say so plainly: “API not published” means integration is possible only under a separate agreement with the network. Promising otherwise would be dishonest.
landing.regulatoryLead: This is not a forecast — these are acts in force and published plans. Integrations for them are scheduled in advance.
landing.rev.bondarBody: Excel and PDF exports come out of the same view I am looking at. Nothing has to be re-keyed.
landing.rev.counterNote: Yes, it is a joke: there is no such percentage. But that is what a month feels like when not a single refuelling had to be hunted down by hand.
landing.rev.hnatiukBody: Engine hours and coolant temperature come from the truck, not from what the driver says.
landing.rev.hrynchukBody: The first month showed how much fuel was slipping past the books. That was the whole business case.
landing.rev.kovalchukBody: Card limits sit next to actual spending. An overrun shows up the same day, not at the end of the month.
landing.rev.lead: Directors, accountants, dispatchers and mechanics all look at one screen and each of them finds their own part of it.
landing.rev.lysenkoBody: The morning fleet check is five minutes instead of an hour of phone calls.
landing.rev.melnykBody: Kopiykas and millilitres arrive already normalised. Closing the month stopped being an event.
landing.rev.promise: You will be satisfied with our service by all of
landing.rev.romaniukBody: I create the trip here and the driver sees it on their side. I no longer keep two systems open.
landing.rev.savchukBody: The track and the CAN fuel level are on one screen. The question "where is the truck" simply went away.
landing.rev.title: The people who stopped reconciling reports by hand
landing.rev.tkachukBody: OKKO and Shell are finally in one report. Reconciliation used to take a day, now it takes a tab.
landing.rm.h1.rationale: The adapter template is already proven on OKKO and Shell, so every next network is days rather than weeks. The fastest payoff for accounting and the most visible change for the client.
landing.rm.h1.title: The entire fuel network in one report
landing.rm.h2.rationale: A card transaction has to meet the bank statement and the tax invoice automatically. Without that an ERP stays a report rather than accounting.
landing.rm.h2.title: Money and documents close the loop
landing.rm.h3.rationale: What directly saves fuel and working time: real consumption from sensors, routing that accounts for truck dimensions, and a tachograph that reads itself.
landing.rm.h3.title: The road, the equipment and the drivers
landing.rm.h4.rationale: The dates are known in advance, so preparation belongs well ahead of the deadline rather than a month out. In parallel — exports to the BI the finance team already uses.
landing.rm.h4.title: Regulation and analytics
landing.rm.reg0.detail: Large taxpayers file the standard audit file; fuel data is a frequent source of questions.
landing.rm.reg0.title: SAF-T UA and e-audit
landing.rm.reg1.detail: NBU Resolution No. 80 is in force; the transition period for banks ended in early 2026.
landing.rm.reg1.title: Ukrainian open banking
landing.rm.reg2.detail: The electronic consignment note for domestic carriage, with dedicated forms for fuel.
landing.rm.reg2.title: e-TTN becomes mandatory
landing.rm.reg3.detail: Regulation 2020/1056 obliges competent authorities to accept e-CMR — relevant for runs to Poland and Romania.
landing.rm.reg3.title: eFTI: EU authorities accept digital data
landing.roadmapLead: Four horizons ordered by dependencies, not by wishes. The regulatory dates are already known — the queue is planned around them.
landing.scene.an.title: SPEND BY WEEK

landing.step1Desc: OKKO returns amounts in kopiykas and volumes in millilitres, Shell returns YYYYMMDD dates, Ruptela returns raw CAN bus fields.
landing.step2Desc: Each vendor has its own service that maps the response onto one schema and absorbs failures: a dead API yields zeros, not a full-screen error.
landing.step3Desc: The interface receives clean data. Roles, caching and write bans live on the server, so guest mode cannot be bypassed from the browser console.
